claims.explanation: Hydroxyfasudil is a ROCK inhibitor whose downstream effects converge on PI3K/Akt/eNOS signaling and actin cytoskeletal regulation; sensitivity likely reflects dependence on ROCK-driven actomyosin contractility and/or intact PTEN/PI3K-Akt signaling, while resistance may arise from alternative survival pathways or low ROCK pathway activity. The selective killing pattern is best explained by PTEN loss or PI3K pathway activation sensitizing cells to ROCK inhibition, with additional contribution from EGFR/RAS/MAPK-driven cytoskeletal remodeling.

features.basis: PTEN loss activates PI3K/Akt, which hydroxyfasudil modulates via ROCK inhibition; PTEN-mutant lines are enriched among sensitive lines
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K/Akt signaling, potentially increasing dependence on ROCK-regulated cytoskeletal and survival pathways
Higher ROCK1 expression increases dependence on ROCK activity, making cells more sensitive to hydroxyfasudil
EGFR mutations are enriched in sensitive NSCLC lines and may cooperate with ROCK signaling in cytoskeletal remodeling
BRAF mutations appear in several sensitive melanoma lines, possibly linking MAPK-driven cytoskeletal changes to ROCK dependence
KRAS mutations are present in multiple sensitive lines and may increase reliance on ROCK-mediated contractility
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK signaling, which may intersect with ROCK-dependent pathways
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so not a strong discriminator; however, some resistant lines lack TP53 mutations
ARID1A mutations appear in several resistant lines, suggesting chromatin remodeling may buffer ROCK inhibition
KMT2D mutations are enriched in resistant lines, possibly reflecting epigenetic compensation
NF2 mutations appear in resistant lines and may alter Hippo/cytoskeletal signaling to reduce ROCK dependence
CDKN2A mutations are present in several resistant lines, potentially indicating alternative proliferation mechanisms
